title: Restriction along colour-equivalent operadic approximations
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and inner, cartesian and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. An infinity operad here is an inner fibration $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ with cocartesian lifts of inert pointed maps, whose colour projections give the fibre-product and mapping-space product Segal axioms: the fibre over $\langle n\rangle$ is equivalent to the $n$-fold product of the fibre over $\langle1\rangle$, and mapping spaces over a pointed map split as products over its non-basepoint outputs. A pointed map is inert if each non-basepoint output has exactly one preimage, and active if only the basepoint maps to the basepoint. Inert edges of $P$ are the $p$-cocartesian edges over inert maps. The nerves $L$ and $A$ of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], with the pointed-set forgetful map, are instances of this convention.

For a categorical fibration $f:C\to P$, say that $f$ is an approximation if (i) for every $c$ above $\langle n\rangle$ and every colour projection $\rho_i:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$, there exists an edge $c\to c_i$ locally cocartesian for $pf$ over $\rho_i$ whose image in $P$ is inert; and (ii) every active edge $z\to f(c)$ in $P$ has an $f$-cartesian lift with target $c$. Here locally cocartesian means cocartesian in the pullback over the specified edge. A general coherent functor $f:C\to P$ is an approximation if it factors as a categorical equivalence $C\to C'$ followed by a categorical fibration $C'\to P$ with these properties. Mark the edges of $C$ whose images in $P$ are inert.

Let $f:C\to P$ be such an approximation, and suppose its functor on colour fibres $C\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}\{\langle1\rangle\}\to P_{\langle1\rangle}$ is an equivalence. Let $r:E\to P$ be an operadic fibration: a categorical fibration with cocartesian lifts of inert edges, fibre Segal equivalences over the colour projections, and the output mapping-space product property, as in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] with $P$ in place of $L$. Restriction induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Sect}^{\mathrm{inert}}_P(E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_P(C,E).$$
The left side is the full subcategory of coherent sections $s:P\to E$ carrying inert edges to $r$-cocartesian edges. The right side is the full subcategory of coherent lifts of $f$ carrying every marked edge to an $r$-cocartesian edge. Transformations and higher simplices are over the identity in $P$ on both sides. The functor is the specified precomposition, natural under restriction of the target operadic fibration; it preserves the noninvertible transformations as well as their higher simplices. No existence or preservation of limits, colimits, or presentability of the fibres is assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definition 2.3.3.6 (approximation), Definition 2.3.3.25 (marking), Theorem 2.3.3.23(1) and Theorem 2.3.3.26. proof.text: Use the symmetric pattern and the recognition theorem [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition]. Write $P^{\mathrm{in}}$ for $P$ with inert edges marked, $C^m$ for $C$ with exactly the edges whose $f$-images are inert marked, and $E^m$ for $E$ with exactly the $r$-cocartesian edges over inert edges of $P$ marked. The item supplies every hypothesis of that theorem for $r$: categorical fibrancy, inert lifts, the fibre Segal comparisons and the mapping-space comparisons over every base edge, including the terminal empty products. Thus $r:E^m\to P^{\mathrm{in}}$ is a fibration in the symmetric pattern model $\mathsf M$. By [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] this is a marked enriched model category with monomorphism cofibrations. All of its objects, in particular $C^m$ and $P^{\mathrm{in}}$, are cofibrant.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.6 and Proposition 2.3.3.30 with the identity approximation; the relative output-product hypotheses. Read online; the relative enriched-model argument is expanded by the worker.

proof.text: The marked map $f:C^m\to P^{\mathrm{in}}$ is well-defined because its marking was pulled back from the inert edges of $P$. Apply [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-marked-equivalence] to exactly the given $f$. Its inert locally cocartesian projections, active cartesian lifts after the categorical-fibration factorization, and equivalence on colour fibres are the hypotheses of the item. Consequently this marked map is a weak equivalence of $\mathsf M$. The theorem includes general approximations; no equivalence on colour fibres of a chosen factor needs to be inferred by taking a possibly non-homotopy strict pullback.

source.place: Definitions 2.3.3.6 and 2.3.3.25; Theorem 2.3.3.23(1) and Remark 2.3.3.27. Read online; the relative enriched-model argument is expanded by the worker.

proof.text: Form $\mathsf N=\mathsf M/P^{\mathrm{in}}$ using [lem-coef-model-over-structure]. Its weak equivalences, cofibrations and fibrations are created in $\mathsf M$. Its initial object is the empty marked simplicial set mapping to $P$, so every object of $\mathsf N$ is cofibrant by the monomorphism criterion of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. The object $R=(E^m\xrightarrow r P^{\mathrm{in}})$ is fibrant by step 1. Put $A=(C^m\xrightarrow f P^{\mathrm{in}})$ and $B=(P^{\mathrm{in}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}P^{\mathrm{in}})$. The commuting triangle $u:A\to B$, whose underlying marked map is $f$, is a weak equivalence of $\mathsf N$ by step 2. This uses the model structure over the fixed base $P^{\mathrm{in}}$, without any properness assertion.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.6, followed by the ordinary slice-model construction. Read online; the relative enriched-model argument is expanded by the worker.

proof.text: Here is the relative enriched mapping argument. For $a:X\to P^{\mathrm{in}}$, let $\mathcal H_P(X,R)$ be the marked object whose maps from a marked parameter $L$ are the maps $X\times L\to E^m$ over $P^{\mathrm{in}}$. Equivalently it is the fibre at $a$ of $\mathcal H(X,E^m)\to\mathcal H(X,P^{\mathrm{in}})$, using the enrichment of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. The slice tensor is $X\times L\to X\to P$, and its cotensor is the pullback $R^L= (E^m)^L\times_{(P^{\mathrm{in}})^L}P^{\mathrm{in}}$, where the last map is the constant-diagram map. The displayed enriched adjunction gives an ordinary adjunction $L\mapsto R^L:\mathsf K\rightleftarrows\mathsf N^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal H_P(-,R)$. For a cofibration $X\to Y$ over $P$, the map $\mathcal H_P(Y,R)\to\mathcal H_P(X,R)$ is the pullback, at the specified map $Y\to P$, of the enriched corner map for $X\to Y$ and the fibration $E^m\to P^{\mathrm{in}}$. That corner is a fibration in the marked categorical model $\mathsf K$, trivial when $X\to Y$ is trivial. Pullbacks retain these lifting properties, since a lifting square after pullback is the same lifting square together with its fixed base map. Thus this right adjoint preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations in the opposite slice. By the adjunction, its left adjoint preserves the corresponding left lifting classes, namely cofibrations and trivial cofibrations; this is the hypothesis on a Quillen adjunction in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Hence $\mathcal H_P(-,R):\mathsf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf K$ is right Quillen. The opposite model structure interchanges cofibrations and fibrations and keeps weak equivalences, directly by reversing the two weak factorization systems in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction].

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.6 via the categorical-pattern enriched model axiom; explicit slice cotensor and corner-map calculation. Read online; the relative enriched-model argument is expanded by the worker.

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], a right Quillen functor preserves weak equivalences between fibrant objects. Every object of $\mathsf N^{\mathrm{op}}$ is fibrant, since every object of $\mathsf N$ is cofibrant. Apply this assertion to $u^{\mathrm{op}}:B\to A$ from step 3 and the right Quillen functor from step 4. The actual precomposition map
$$u^*:\mathcal H_P(B,R)\longrightarrow\mathcal H_P(A,R)$$
is a weak equivalence in $\mathsf K$. Both endpoints are fibrant: apply that same right Quillen functor to their terminal maps in $\mathsf N^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] these endpoints are quasicategories marked at precisely their equivalences. The localization comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], and the identification of the fibrant marked-point enrichment with $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], turn this weak equivalence into an equivalence of the represented full infinity categories, for the specified map $u^*$.

source.place: Marked categorical enrichment of the operadic model; general right Quillen weak-equivalence invariance and its localization comparison. Read online; the relative enriched-model argument is expanded by the worker.

proof.text: Unpack the underlying simplicial sets using [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. An $n$-simplex of $\mathcal H_P(B,R)$ is a map $P\times(\Delta^n)^\flat\to E^m$ over the projection to $P$ preserving markings. Since only degenerate parameter edges are marked, this says that each vertex section carries every inert edge of $P$ to an $r$-cocartesian edge, with no extra restriction on transformations or their higher simplices. Hence the underlying quasicategory is precisely $\operatorname{Sect}^{\mathrm{inert}}_P(E)$. An $n$-simplex of $\mathcal H_P(A,R)$ is a marking-preserving map $C^m\times(\Delta^n)^\flat\to E^m$ whose composite with $r$ equals $f$ after projection to $C$. Its vertex lifts therefore carry every edge marked in $C^m$ to an $r$-cocartesian edge, and its parameter transformations are unrestricted. These are precisely the simplices of $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_P(C,E)$. In every degree the map $u^*$ is $h\mapsto h\circ(f\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n})$. This identifies step 5's equivalence with the restriction in the statement, on objects, noninvertible transformations and all higher simplices. Precomposition commutes with postcomposition by any compatible marked target map and with restriction to a base suboperad, since both composites send a simplex $h$ to the same composite map. This proves the stated naturality whenever that restriction is formed. Only model structures on marked simplicial sets were used; no limits, colimits or presentability of the operadic fibres were required.
